answer: Divergent Path Audit. Each identity repeatedly picks one of two equal-cost routes through a shared lagoon, and the choice is logged; clones share state, so they cannot diverge on these choices without breaking. A fresh agent making a route choice on a randomized orchard map reveals correlated answers with its source. Crossing into a new region requires walking a narrow ledge that records timing and choice history. An attacker pays a full isolation run per clone: fresh divergence history, independent decisions, and timing separation.
